skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging

skills.name: kernel-development

skills.name: library-development

skills.name: test

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. //==================================================================================================
4. // Modules
5. //==================================================================================================
6. 
7. use vstd::prelude::*;
8. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
9. include!("mod.spec.rs");
10. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
11. include!("mod.proof.rs");
12. 
13. mod flags;
14. mod frame;
15. mod pde;
16. mod pte;
17. mod table;
18. 
19. //==================================================================================================
20. // Exports
21. //==================================================================================================
22. 
23. pub use flags::*;
24. pub use frame::FrameNumber;
25. pub use pde::*;
26. pub use pte::*;
27. pub use table::*;
28. 
29. //==================================================================================================
30. // Types
31. //==================================================================================================
32. 
33. ///
34. /// # Description
35. ///
36. /// Word type for page table entries (32-bit on x86).
37. ///
38. pub type PteWord = u32;
39. 
40. ///
41. /// # Description
42. ///
43. /// Log2 of the size of [`PteWord`] in bytes.
44. ///
45. pub const PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2: usize = ::core::mem::size_of::<PteWord>().trailing_zeros() as usize;
46. 
47. ///
48. /// # Description
49. ///
50. /// Number of page-sized pages reserved for the root paging hierarchy on x86.
51. ///
52. /// On 32-bit x86 with non-PAE paging, this corresponds to one page directory.
53. ///
54. pub const NUM_HIERARCHY_PAGES: usize = 1;
55. 
56. //==================================================================================================
57. // Standalone Functions
58. //==================================================================================================
59. 
60. ///
61. /// # Description
62. ///
63. /// Flushes the TLB entry for the page containing `vaddr`.
64. ///
65. /// # Safety
66. ///
67. /// Must be called from kernel mode (ring 0).
68. ///
69. // Trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md` and the module's
70. // `verus-unsupported.md`): the body is a single `core::arch::asm!` block issuing the
71. // `invlpg` instruction, which flushes the CPU TLB entry for `vaddr`. Verus does not
72. // support inline-asm expressions, so the body cannot be verified. The effect is purely
73. // on hardware TLB state — outside Verus' memory model and invisible to every caller's
74. // Rust-visible state — so the faithful contract is empty (no `requires`, trivial
75. // `ensures`): any `usize` is accepted, no error path, and no Rust-visible state changes,
76. // hence every caller-side invariant is preserved. This matches the inherited upstream
77. // `assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::paging::invlpg ]` (no `requires`/`ensures`).
78. #[inline]
79. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
80. pub unsafe fn invlpg(vaddr: usize) {
81.     core::arch::asm!(
82.         "invlpg ({0})",
83.         in(reg) vaddr,
84.         options(nostack, preserves_flags, att_syntax)
85.     );
86. }
87.
